source_lines_after.32: For $C_n=\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^n,-\lVert\cdot\rVert^2)$, a finite-dimensional graded real module $M=M^0\oplus M^1$ determines the ABS symbol triple $(\pi^*M^0,\pi^*M^1,c(v))$ on the disk/sphere pair of $\mathbb{R}^n$: over a nonzero vector $v$, Clifford multiplication $c(v)$ is an isomorphism because $c(v)^2=-\lVert v\rVert^2I$. Its relative KO class is the candidate symbol. The separate theorem proves that the symbol vanishes on restrictions from $C_{n+1}$, descends to $A_n$, and is an isomorphism.
source_lines_after.34: The symbol is a relative class on the disk/sphere pair; since $c(v)$ is invertible for $v\ne0$, the triple is admissible. This definition alone does not claim factorization through $A_n$.
